3.PID

includes:

-Endometritis
-Salpingitis
-Oophoritis
-Tubo – ovarian abscess
-Pelvic peritonitis.

D/D:

•UTI
•Ectopic
•Ovarian cyst complications.
•Appendicitis
•Functional pain
•Endometriosis

Causative Agents:

•3% gonococcal
•14 – 35% CT ¼ of PiD in UK
•4 – 6 weeks after IUCD

Others:

-Gardnella
-Anaerobes
-Mycoplasma – emerging agent.

Symptoms:

•Lower abdominal pain
•Deep dyspareunia
•AUB
-IMB
-PCB
-Menorrhagia.
•Abnormal discharge

Signs:

•B/L tenderness in lower abdomen
•Adnexal tenderness
•Cervical motion tenderness
•Fever > 380 C.

Diagnosis:

•Clinical S/S => PPV 65 – 90%
•Elevated ESR, CRP
•Testing for NG & CT.
•Absence of PUS cells on endo cervical & vaginal swabs => Good NPV 95% but presence has PPV of 17%.

Management:

•Don’t delay – risk of complication
-Subfertility
-Ectopic
-CPP
-Fitz hugh Curtis syndrome
•Empirical treatment.
•Rest
•Analgesia
•Avoid intercourse till they & their partners have completed treatment.
•Partner screening is recommended
•OCP + Break through bleeding => STI screening esp CT.
•UPT => Offer
•Screening for STI including HIV => offer

Out Patient Treatment (Mild – Moderate):

1.Ceftriaxone 1g stat IM

+ Doxi 100mg

+ Flagyl 400 B.D

2.Ofloxacin 400 B.D

+ metronidazole

3.Ceftriaxone 1g stat I/M

+ Azthro 1g/weeks. [14 DAYS]

4.Oral Moxi 400 OD – [14 DAYS]

 

⇨M-Genitalium = moxifloxacin
⇨Pregnancy, B.F – parental therapy.
⇨Severe PID – Consider anaerobes
⇨Quinolones – avoided in Gonococcal PID due to ing resistance.
⇨Don’t use Quinolones as 1st line
⇨I/V in inpatient regimens should be continued 24 hours after clinical improvement.
⇨Partner treatment:
1.Azthro 1g – single dose.
2.Screening in 6m0 duration
3.Avoid sexual intercourse until index pt have completed treatment course.

TOC:

•2 – 4 weeks.
•CT – not routinely if indicated then after 3 – 5weeks.

In – Patient:

•Surgical Emergency can’t be excluded.
•No response to therapy
•Severe disease
•To Abscess
•Intolerance to oral treatment
•Pregnancy
1.Ceftriaxone 2g daily I/v + Doxi B.D.

Followed by

Doxi B.D

+ Metronidazole B.D

2.Clinda 90mg TDS

+ Gentamycin 2mg/kg loading dose then 1.5mg/kg 1day – TDS

F.B

Oral clinda 45mg QDS or

Doxi 10mg B.D

+ Metronidazole

Gentamycin levels should be monitored.

3.I/V ofloxacin 400mg B.D + I/V

Metronidazole 500mg TDS – 14days

4.Cipro 200 B.D + Doxi + Metronidazole TID = 14 days.

Surgical management:

⇨Laparoscopy – divide adhesions & drainage of pelvic abscess.
⇨USG Guided aspiration of fluid collection is less invasive but equally effective.
⇨Adhesiolysis in Perihepatitis.

Follow Up:

⇨72 hours in moderate – severe.
⇨Further review 2 – 4 weeks.

Persistent symptoms, consider

-I/V antibiotics
-Rule out resistance.

-Recurrent infection.

Repeat testing for N.G & CT after 2 – 4 weeks.
